blocks.text: Managing high volume email as a claims adjuster

Your inbox is the center of your claims management process. When you handle dozens of files, every email is a potential piece of evidence or a status request. The goal is to move from reactive reading to active filing. Start by creating a folder structure that matches your claim numbering system. Use the Outlook menu at the top of your screen to select File > New > Folder. Name it by the claim number or the claimant name. This keeps your main inbox clear for new, urgent requests.
Using rules to automate your inbox

Rules are your best friend for sorting documents. If you receive automated status updates from a specific vendor, create a rule to move them into a dedicated folder immediately. Go to Tools > Rules > Edit Rules. Click the plus sign to add a new rule. Set the condition to look for the sender's email address. Set the action to move the message to your folder. This ensures that you only see items that need your direct attention in your main inbox.
Faster with Lazur

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you manage Outlook without digging through menus. When you are stuck or need to find a setting, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask. It answers out loud, saving you time. If you need to write a long email to a claimant, hold the fn key to dictate your response. Lazur formats your speech into clear, professional text at your cursor.
Keyboard shortcuts for claims adjusters

Keyboard shortcuts cut down on mouse movement. Use ⌘ + 1 to switch to Mail, ⌘ + 2 for Calendar, and ⌘ + 3 for Contacts. If you need to create a new email, hit ⌘ + N. To send an email, use ⌘ + Return. These small habits add up over a day of processing 100 emails. If you find yourself forgetting these, ask Lazur to remind you of the shortcut for a specific action.

If a shortcut does not work, check your System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts. Microsoft Outlook for Mac does not have a native menu for changing these, so you must add them manually here.

blocks.text: Maintaining an audit trail

Compliance requires that every interaction is documented. Do not leave emails sitting in your inbox for weeks. Once you have read an email and taken action, move it to the relevant claim folder. If you have an email that requires a follow-up, use the flag feature. Right-click the email and select Follow Up. This keeps the item on your radar without cluttering your workspace.
Handling attachments and documents

Claims adjusters deal with many attachments like medical reports or photos. Do not keep these inside Outlook. Drag them to your local Mac folders on your desktop or your secure cloud drive. This keeps your Outlook database size manageable and ensures your files are backed up properly. If you struggle to find where a file went, use the search bar in Outlook with filters like 'hasattachments:yes' to narrow down your list.
Communication with vendors and claimants

Your tone must remain professional regardless of the situation. Use signatures in Outlook to save time. Go to Outlook > Settings > Signatures. Create a standard signature that includes your contact information and your claim department details. This ensures that every email you send has the necessary information for the recipient to reach you.
Troubleshooting sync issues

Connectivity errors like -3253 can halt your work. If this happens, check your internet connection first. Then, try restarting Outlook. If the problem persists, go to the Help menu and select Check for Updates to ensure you are on the latest version. As of late 2026, Microsoft requires macOS 14 or later for full support. If you are on an older OS, you may face stability issues.
Why adjusters choose Mac

The Mac ecosystem provides a stable environment for multitasking. You can easily drag files between your browser-based claims system and your email client. Using Split View by hovering over the green window button allows you to see your claim file on one side and your Outlook inbox on the other. This visual layout helps you compare data without switching windows constantly.
What to do when you get stuck

When you are in the middle of a complex claim, you cannot afford to stop and search for help. Use Lazur to keep your momentum. If you need to know how to create a rule for a new claim, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask. Lazur will guide you through the menu paths. If you need to dictate a long note for a file, hold the fn key. It captures your thoughts accurately so you can move to the next claim.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to automatically file my emails?
faq.answer: Lazur does not click buttons or move files for you. However, you can ask Lazur to guide you through the process of setting up Outlook rules so that your emails are sorted automatically.

faq.question: Is Outlook for Mac stable for high-volume claims work?
faq.answer: Yes, provided you keep the app updated and run it on a supported version of macOS. Most performance issues stem from outdated software or sync errors with the mail server.

faq.question: How do I manage my calendar alongside my inbox?
faq.answer: Use ⌘ + 2 to switch to your calendar. You can drag an email onto the calendar icon to create a meeting invite automatically. This is a fast way to schedule field visits or follow-up calls.
